rows.title: How to start a bank
rows.standfirst: In some ways, starting a bank is a lot like starting any other business. Who will you hire? Where will you be located? What color will the couches be? But it's also way more complicated. There are tons of regulations on banks–and you can understand why. Lots of new businesses fail. But if a bank fails, it can have ripple effects for the entire economy.

rows.title: Top Democrats ask Rubio for answers on now-canceled $400 million Tesla plan
rows.standfirst: A letter from two House Democrats presses Rubio for details about who approved an effort to try to use hundreds of millions of dollars of taxpayer money on armored electric vehicles from Tesla.

rows.title: Can ... we still trust the monthly jobs report?
rows.standfirst: Between the Trump administration wanting to change how GDP is calculated and DOGE accessing sensitive government information, statistical agencies are under the microscope. Can we still trust official numbers like the monthly jobs report? A former Bureau of Labor Statistics commissioner shares her worries about the future integrity of government data.

rows.title: The job market is still pretty solid — but there are warning signs ahead
rows.standfirst: U.S. employers added 151,000 jobs in February, while the unemployment rate inched up to 4.1% from 4.0% in January.

rows.title: A look at some of the creative ways companies try to dodge high tariffs
rows.standfirst: Companies can try to avoid or minimize tariffs by requesting exemptions or legally reclassifying their products. Here's a look at some of the strategies that have worked in the past.

rows.title: Farmers strongly back Trump. A new trade war could test their loyalty
rows.standfirst: American farmers have stood firmly behind President Trump even when his trade policies hurt them. The latest trade war, which could be even worse for their sector, promises to test those ties again.

rows.title: 'A blitz attack': VA mental health experts liken Elon Musk's emails to warfare
rows.standfirst: Mental health professionals with the Veterans Health Administration say the stress caused by Elon Musk's "What did you do last week?" emails is hurting veterans' care.

rows.title: Trump pledges support for crypto sector at White House summit
rows.standfirst: President Trump signed an order creating a cryptocurrency strategic reserve using bitcoin seized through court proceedings, and directing officials to find "budget-neutral" ways to grow it.

rows.title: 5 takeaways: China's foreign minister slams Trump's 'two-faced' policies
rows.standfirst: China's top foreign policy official addressed the escalating trade war with the U.S. and promoted China as an "anchor" on the global stage as America retreats from international involvement.

rows.title: Walgreens agrees to be acquired by private equity firm for almost $10 billion
rows.standfirst: A buyout to take the drugstore chain private would give it more flexibility to make changes to improve its business without worrying about Wall Street's reaction.

rows.title: SpaceX's latest Starship test flight ends with another explosion
rows.standfirst: Nearly two months after an explosion sent flaming debris raining down on the Turks and Caicos, SpaceX launched another mammoth Starship rocket but lost contact minutes into the test flight.

rows.title: When it comes to the economy, it's all about uncertainty
rows.standfirst: Like a lot of economists, Mark Zandi, with Moody's Analytics, thinks President Trump's across-the-board tariffs are a bad idea. Saying, "Tariffs, broad-based tariffs, are a real problem for the economy."

rows.title: Trump's latest tariff twist: A break for Mexico and Canada
rows.standfirst: Trump put 25% tariffs on goods from Canada and Mexico on Tuesday. Markets tanked. And by Thursday, he had decided to broadly lift them.

rows.title: At a housewares expo in Chicago, talk keeps turning to price hikes from tariffs
rows.standfirst: The Inspired Home Show in Chicago draws housewares industry insiders from all over the country to network and show off their latest gadgets. This year, they're making plans to cope with tariffs.

rows.title: Did tariffs contribute to the Great Depression? Here's what to know
rows.standfirst: Several factors led to the Great Depression, one of the most severe economic crises in U.S. history. NPR interviewed economists who discussed the causes of the Great Depression.

rows.title: Tesla, led by Elon Musk, warns of export retaliation due to new Trump tariffs
rows.standfirst: Tesla has joined the ranks of U.S. companies concerned that Trump's aggressive tariff policies may negatively affect global sales.

rows.title: Trump says the economy is in 'transition.' What comes after?
rows.standfirst: "A little disturbance," "a period of transition," "a detox period." These are all phrases that President Trump and his administration have used to describe the economy, as the stock market has plunged in response to one tariff announcement after another.

rows.title: How Tupperware took over our homes, with Decoder Ring
rows.standfirst: Tupperware is the stealthy star of our modern homes. These plastic storage containers are ubiquitous in our fridges, pantries, and closets. But the original product was revolutionary. So was its breakthrough sales strategy: the Tupperware Party.

rows.title: FTC asks to delay Amazon trial over 'dire' resources, then quickly backtracks
rows.standfirst: The Federal Trade Commission is in a "dire resource situation," a federal lawyer said on a call about its major lawsuit against Amazon. Within hours, he retracted the claim.

rows.title: Dorothy Thompson: The journalist who warned us about Hitler
rows.standfirst: Dorothy Thompson saw the rise of Nazi Germany as a foreign correspondent in Berlin. A new series from Radio Diaries tells the story of Thompson's career as a radio broadcaster.

rows.title: Why CEOs are calm about tariffs in public — but 'very discouraged' in private
rows.standfirst: Business leaders are trying to engage in a delicate diplomacy with the White House — even as their companies brace for the impact of market volatility and tariffs.

rows.title: Southwest surprises, tariff guac shock, and fraud flourishes
rows.standfirst: It's Indicators of the Week! Our weekly look at interesting numbers from the news.

rows.title: A 2nd judge orders thousands of fired federal employees temporarily reinstated
rows.standfirst: A federal judge in Maryland found the Trump administration acted unlawfully in firing thousands of federal employees by not first notifying states.

rows.title: (Don't) click here to pay your tolls: How you can stop spam texts
rows.standfirst: "Smishing" scams aim to compromise your data and pilfer money. And if you think the problem is getting worse, you're right.

rows.title: Donatella Versace to step down as brand's chief creative officer after nearly 30 years
rows.standfirst: Donatella took over the brand after the murder of her brother, Gianni Versace, its founder, in 1997. Her bold creative vision and unique style have been instrumental in preserving the Versace legacy.

rows.title: As global tariff tensions rise, here's the latest on U.S. trade with top partners
rows.standfirst: President Trump has upended global markets by imposing tariffs on imports from several of America's top trading partners. Here's what to know.

rows.title: Elon Musk is winning Republican fans. Can Tesla win them over, too?
rows.standfirst: Tesla is gaining traction among conservative buyers, while it loses support among liberals. But are there enough Republican EV shoppers to make up the difference?

rows.title: Trump threatens a 200% tariff on European alcohol
rows.standfirst: European wines, champagne and other beverages could face heavy tariffs if Trump follows through with this threat.

rows.title: Judge dismisses Fox News from sexual assault lawsuit against former star
rows.standfirst: A federal judge has dismissed Fox News as a defendant in a lawsuit filed against former anchor Ed Henry. Former producer Jennifer Eckhart alleges he sexually harassed and raped her.

rows.title: Curious about buy-now, pay-later loans? Here are 6 pros and cons
rows.standfirst: Called "buy-now, pay-later" loans, they essentially work the way they sound. Shoppers borrow money to buy goods then pay the loan back over time, often interest-free. Experts share risks and benefits.

rows.title: Voice of America journalists sue Trump administration for shutting down network
rows.standfirst: Six Voice of America journalists and a director at its parent agency have sued the Trump administration, alleging its moves to shut down the U.S.-funded network are unconstitutional.

rows.title: What's the ideal age to reach a life milestone? Many Americans say it depends
rows.standfirst: Owning a home, starting a family or retiring: If these are things you want, what's the best age to do them? The Pew Research Center surveyed 3,600 U.S. adults to find out.

rows.title: Can we just change how we measure GDP?
rows.standfirst: There's one statistic that rules them all when it comes to keeping track of the economy: gross domestic product (GDP). It's the sum of all final transactions, so all the goods or services bought and sold, in an economy. GDP tells us how hot the economy is running, or how cool — like if we might be heading into a recession. And it's an important tool to compare countries, policies, and politicians. It's used by the U.S. government to allocate money and by businesses to make decisions about the future.

rows.title: Whistleblower John Barnett's family files wrongful death suit against Boeing
rows.standfirst: The lawsuit includes a photo of a notebook found in John Barnett's truck when he died by suicide, bearing the message, "I pray Boeing Pays!!!" In response to the new lawsuit, Boeing said in a statement, "We are saddened by John Barnett's death and extend our condolences to his family."

rows.title: How Trump's firings could upend a 90-year-old Supreme Court ruling limiting his power
rows.standfirst: Already, lower courts have found President Trump's removal of Democratic members of independent agencies to be unlawful. The Trump administration has appealed.

rows.title: A new-ish gold rush and other indicators
rows.standfirst: It's Indicators of the Week! Our weekly look at interesting numbers from the news.

rows.title: Farming is uncertain — a trade war makes it more so
rows.standfirst: Farmers already worry about things like crop prices, the cost of farm supplies and extreme weather.

rows.title: Ben & Jerry's alleges its CEO was fired over its political activism. Here's the scoop
rows.standfirst: Ben & Jerry's alleges its parent company, Unilever, ousted its CEO in retaliation for social media posts supporting progressive causes. The last few years have been a rocky road for the companies.

rows.title: The Fed holds interest rates. And, judge denies request to block DOGE's USIP takeover
rows.standfirst: The Federal Reserve held interest rates steady yesterday as concerns loom over President Trump's new tariffs. And, a judge denied a request to block DOGE's takeover of the U.S. Institute of Peace.

rows.title: With Trump's crackdown on DEI, some women fear a path to good-paying jobs will close
rows.standfirst: Some fear a setback for women and people of color after President Trump revoked a 1965 executive order that required federal contractors to identify and address barriers to employment.

rows.title: The Federal Trade Commission keeps tabs on big business. Trump fired 2 of its members
rows.standfirst: President Trump fired two Democratic appointees from the independent agency tasked with policing corporate America. One of them told NPR the move is a gift to the president's wealthiest supporters.

rows.title: What's this about a crypto reserve?
rows.standfirst: In 2009, Bitcoin launched as the first cryptocurrency. Just under two decades, President Trump has signed an executive order to create the "Strategic Bitcoin Reserve and United States Digital Asset Stockpile." On today's show, we look at what the U.S. government plans for this new strategy, plus who benefits from a crypto reserve.

rows.title: Trump is taking a hammer to traditional pillars of soft power
rows.standfirst: The argument for international aid is in part a moral one, but it's also been about U.S. interests. As then-senator Marco Rubio put it in 2017: "I promise you it's going to be a lot harder to recruit someone to anti-Americanism, anti-American terrorism if the United States of America was the reason why they're even alive today."

rows.title: The Fed holds interest rates steady as Trump's trade agenda sparks uncertainty
rows.standfirst: The Fed held rates steady, but left the door open to cut them later this year if inflation continues to ease. Trump's tariffs, however, could complicate efforts to bring prices under control.

rows.title: It's your last chance to claim pandemic-era stimulus checks, the IRS says. Here's how
rows.standfirst: The IRS says some Americans who have not filed their 2021 tax returns could be eligible for a pandemic-era relief payment, as long as they do so by April 15. Here's what to know as Tax Day approaches.

rows.title: Hyundai's plans for its new Georgia plant reveal an industry hedging its bets on EVs
rows.standfirst: Hyundai just opened a high-tech auto plant in Georgia. Originally meant to just build EVs, it's expanding toward plug-in hybrids — a sign of bigger shifts in the auto industry.

rows.title: Overly Friendly Emails and other marketing pet peeves
rows.standfirst: Brands trying to be your best bud. Generational labels. Gendered double standards.

rows.title: Asian shares are sharply lower over concerns about the U.S. economy
rows.standfirst: Asian shares were sharply lower on Monday as worries are building over a potentially toxic mix of worsening inflation and a U.S. economy slowing because households are cautious to spend.

rows.title: Gambling with Memes
rows.standfirst: What do Moo Deng the pygmy hippo, social media sensation Hawk Tuah, and the President of the United States all have in common? They've all inspired highly valuable, highly volatile memecoins. The memecoin began as a sort of joke cryptocurrency, but it soon became very real.

rows.title: FCC chair opens investigation into Disney and ABC over DEI practices
rows.standfirst: FCC chair Brendan Carr said he wants a review all of Disney's DEI practices — both past and present — to determine whether the company has ever violated any FCC regulations.

rows.title: Startup founder convicted of defrauding JPMorgan Chase of $175M by faking firm's success
rows.standfirst: Charlie Javice, whose startup claimed to be revolutionizing the way college students apply for financial aid, was convicted of defrauding the banking giant by exaggerating her customer base tenfold.

rows.title: From Seattle to Miami, anti-Musk protesters gather at hundreds of Tesla locations
rows.standfirst: At a rally in Los Angeles, 65-year-old Phil Ansell said he wanted to participate because "I want to do everything possible to protect democracy in this country."

rows.title: Judicial rulings block Kari Lake's drive to shutter Voice of America
rows.standfirst: Trump senior adviser Kari Lake is regrouping after U.S. judges blocked her from taking further actions against the Voice of America and Radio Free Europe/Radio Liberty.

rows.title: Federal judge prevents Trump administration from dismantling CFPB
rows.standfirst: The temporary injunction issued by Judge Berman Jackson seeks to preserve the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau as a lawsuit filed by the agency's union proceeds.

rows.title: Appeals court rules Trump can fire board members of independent agencies
rows.standfirst: The D.C. Circuit Court of Appeals ruled 2-1 that Trump can fire Democratic members of the National Labor Relations Board and the Merit Systems Protection Board after a lower court had them reinstated.

rows.title: Trump's changes to a $42 billion broadband program could be a win for Musk's Starlink
rows.standfirst: After years of planning, the Trump administration is overhauling a federal universal broadband initiative to open the door to Musk's Starlink satellite service.

rows.title: PM x Radiolab: Can the economy grow forever?
rows.standfirst: Earth can sustain life for another 100 million years, but can we? This episode, we partner with Radiolab to take stock of the essential raw materials that enable us to live as we do here on Earth — everything from sand to copper to oil — and tally up how much we have left. Are we living with reckless abandon? And if so, is there even a way to stop? A simultaneously terrifying and delightful conversation about bird poop, daredevil drivers, and some staggering back-of-the-envelope math.

rows.title: Trump signs order ending union bargaining rights for wide swaths of federal employees
rows.standfirst: President Trump's new executive order ends collective bargaining for wide swaths of federal employees, as part of his broader campaign to reshape the government's workforce. Unions are vowing to sue.

rows.title: U.S. sees large rise in border seizures of eggs, while fentanyl rate falls
rows.standfirst: President Trump cites risks from fentanyl to justify tariffs on Canada and Mexico. U.S. Customs and Border Protection says interceptions of eggs are way up, compared to 63 fentanyl cases last month.

rows.title: Missing taxes, spiking copper and Napster's re-re-rebirth
rows.standfirst: On Indicators of the Week, we look at a huge projected tax shortfall, the price of copper and the afterlife of Napster, the peer-to-peer file-sharing service that refuses to die.
